title: Woodburn suspends Flock Safety license plate cameras amid concerns of federal ICE enforcement - Woodburn Independent
summary: The city of Woodburn, Oregon suspended its Flock Safety license-plate camera system for at least two months after residents at a Nov. 10 council meeting raised concerns the cameras could aid federal immigration enforcement. The city will conduct a comprehensive review during the pause; officials said access is limited to Oregon law enforcement and that Oregon sanctuary laws bar cooperation with ICE.

key_quotes.quote: Based on community input, pausing the Flock camera system is a prudent step.
Our goal is to ensure that the system is used responsibly, that the information collected remains secure, and that it is not accessible to any agency outside of Oregon

We demand an audit of the use of the flock cameras. And then the audit must include the number of requests made by other agencies, FBI, ICE, (U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration) and other federal agencies.
Our police have never worked with ICE agents. They will not work with any ICE agents.
